recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Reverting to the exact 2015 'codes' wording would be less accurate for the current model, while the current 'values representing permitted answers' wording satisfies the original clarification without adding redundant prose.
issue_request: FHIR-6810 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 Patient Care request to clarify Questionnaire.group.question.options. The accepted resolution changed the description from a vague reference to possible options to a value set containing codes representing permitted answers for the question.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in SVN r5941, represented by git commit 26e8b597d5034f4372a848e5660a88268f4b664c, which changed the old Questionnaire.group.question.options short text and definition from possible options to permitted answers and listed issue #6810 in the commit subject.
additional_context: Questionnaire is active in the current build and source/fhir.ini maps the old Questionnaire.item.options name to Questionnaire.item.answerValueSet. Later Published issue FHIR-20396 reworked Questionnaire choice/open-choice handling for R5, added answerConstraint, and broadened answerValueSet wording from codes to values, which fits the current coding/string/uri-capable model.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change is needed because source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml already defines Questionnaire.item.answerValueSet as a ValueSet containing permitted answers and as a list of values representing permitted answers for a question.
